simple: Every Roblox account has a number that identifies it, called a user ID. Roblox is changing things so that each game gets its own private ID number for each player, called a domain-scoped user ID. So the same player has one number in your game and a different number in someone else's game. This page shows how to use the `User` type in your scripts so your saves, badges, and leaderboards keep working.
analogy: It is like a school giving you a student number. Your number at your school is different from your number at a summer camp, even though you are the same person. Each place only understands its own number.
keyPoints: A User is your Roblox account. A Player is that account while it is inside a running game server.
New players get a different ID number in every game, so an ID only makes sense inside the game that gave it out.
Players who joined your game before this change keep their old global ID in your game, so old saves still work.
Get a player's `User` value with `player.User`. It has `Id`, `DomainType`, and `DomainId`.
Engine functions that take a user ID, like `BadgeService:AwardBadge()`, also accept a `User` value, and Roblox recommends passing the `User`.
For data store keys inside one game, use `player.User.Id`. To save the full identity for other systems, use `user:ToString()` and later `User.fromString()`.
Use `Player` for things during the session (movement, GUI, chat) and `User` for identity that lasts (saves, cross-game references).
Never use an ID number from one game to find a player in a different game.

terms.user ID: A number that identifies a Roblox account. For example, a player might be `123` in one game.
terms.domain: The place an ID belongs to, such as one specific game or one outside app. An ID only means something inside its own domain.
terms.domain-scoped user ID: An ID number that only works inside one game or app. The same player could be `500789` in Game B and `302441` in Game C.
terms.global user ID: The older kind of ID that was the same in every game. Returning players keep this one in games they already played.
terms.Datatype: A built-in kind of value in Luau, like `Vector3` or `User`. It is a value, not an object you see in the Explorer.
terms.DomainType: An enum that says what kind of domain the ID belongs to: `EXPERIENCE` (a game) or `OAUTH` (an outside app).
terms.serialize: Turn a value into text so it can be saved or sent somewhere, then turned back later. `ToString()` serializes a `User`.
terms.collide: When two different things accidentally get the same number. Scoped IDs never collide with global IDs.
terms.session: One visit to a server, from when a player joins until they leave.

example.title: Print a player's IDs and make a save key
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	-- The User value for this player in this game
	local user = player.User
	print(player.Name, "has ID", user.Id, "in this game")

	-- A data store key that only needs to work inside this game
	local key = ("player_%d"):format(user.Id)
	print("Save key:", key)

	-- Full identity as text, safe to store for other systems
	local encoded = user:ToString()
	print("Saved as text:", encoded)
end)
explain: When a player joins, `PlayerAdded` runs the function and hands it the `player`.
`player.User` gives you the `User` value for that player in your game.
`user.Id` is the number for that player in this game only. It builds a save key like `player_500789`.
`user:ToString()` turns the whole identity into text, which you can turn back with `User.fromString()` later.

watchOut: Do not copy a player's ID from your game and use it in another game or tool. The number will point to nobody, or to someone else.
Do not panic about old saves. Players who joined before the change keep their old ID in your game.
Use `ToString()` and `User.fromString()` when you save a full `User`, not your own homemade format.
